item.title: Cycling in Denmark, explained
item.description: You won’t catch me on a bike in the endless winter months, but apparently 80% of Danes still bike, rain or shine, frost or snow. This does not surprise me, when you think that nothing stopped the Vikings from getting into open boats and crossing the Atlantic in all weathers, writes Vivienne McKee.

item.title: Hald Thorup wins Denmark’s first medal at the Winter Olympics
item.description: Danish speedskater Viktor Hald Thorup made history by winning silver in the men’s mass start, securing Denmark’s first-ever individual Winter Olympic medal. Hald Thorup established an early breakaway with Dutchman Jorrit Bergsma, which the field failed to catch after starting their pursuit too late. item.title: Also in Christiania, finding a place to live is not easy anymore. This is how the Free City is – and has been – according to a person who has lived there for decades
item.description: After four decades in Christiania, one resident reflects on how the freetown has changed, from easier housing and internal tensions to growing tourism, new residents and shifting priorities.

item.title: Denmark warns about puff bars and vapes after death
item.description: The Danish Health Authority is warning against illegal liquids for puff bars and e-cigarettes following a death caused by poisoning with a synthetic cannabinoid. According to forensic experts at Aarhus University, the death involved the illegal substance 5F-ADB. Even small amounts of this lab-made chemical can be fatal. item.title: Reconstruction of Børsen opens to the public
item.description: On Thursday, a visitor center opens at the Børsen construction site, allowing the public to follow the reconstruction after the 2024 fire. Owned by Dansk Erhverv, the center consists of 15 elevated containers overlooking the site. Visitors can explore the 400-year history of King Christian IV’s iconic building and view artifacts such as charred beams […]

item.title: Government adds billions to Ukraine fund in economic plan
item.description: The Danish government’s economic plan until 2035 proposes an additional 3.8 billion DKK for the Ukraine Fund. Defense Minister Troels Lund Poulsen stated that supporting Ukraine’s defense contributes to the security of Europe and Denmark. Including revenue from F-16 sales, Denmark’s total contribution to Ukraine will reach 14 billion DKK this year, bringing defense spending […]

item.title: Greenland to hit minus 65 degrees next week
item.description: The Danish Meteorological Institute reports that temperatures on Greenland’s ice sheet reached minus 50 degrees Celsius on Sunday, with forecasts predicting minus 65 degrees by Wednesday. item.title: Greenland PM rejects Trump’s hospital ship
item.description: Greenland has rejected U.S. President Donald Trump’s plan to send a hospital ship to the island. Jens-Frederik Nielsen, head of the Greenlandic government, responded with a “no thank you,” highlighting that Greenland offers free public healthcare. Nielsen emphasized that decisions regarding Greenland are made locally and urged for direct dialogue rather than social media outbursts. […]

item.title: Three in four Ukrainians want to stay in Denmark
item.description: A new analysis by the Rockwool Foundation and the University of Copenhagen reveals that 76 percent of Ukrainians living in Denmark want to stay, even if their hometowns were no longer affected by war. item.title: Pharma industry drives Danish economic growth
item.description: According to Statistics Denmark, the Danish economy grew by 2.9% in 2025. The pharmaceutical industry remains a major driver; while Gross Value Added increased by 3.2%, growth would have been only 1.7% without this sector’s contribution.
